Notebook introduction

This document provides a comprehensive technical reference for the 3D surface morphing architecture, Manim-style studio illumination, polyhedra edge treatment, and real-time programmatic vertex deformation systems in Retiam.
1. Architectural Overview & Design Philosophy
Retiam supports two complementary paradigms for animating 3D geometry in WebGPU:

blocks.text: 2. Manim-Style 3D Surface Shading vs. PBR Rendering
Retiam provides two rendering modes for 3D surfaces and models:
2.1 The Two Shading Pipelines Compared

cells.text: Microfacet Cook-Torrance BRDF (GGX distribution, Smith geometry, Fresnel-Schlick)
Three-point studio illumination (Key light, Fill light, High ambient floor)
~120+ shader ALU instructions, multi-texture lookups, environment BRDF LUTs
~15 lightweight ALU arithmetic instructions, zero texture fetches
Signature dual-tone alternating checkerboard quads (or solid)
Clean mathematical diagrams, expository animations, ribbon/sheet morphs

blocks.text: 2.2 The Manim Lighting Equation
The mathematical lighting formulation implemented in `ManimSurfaceFragment` is:

items: **Key Light ($\vec{L}_{\text{key}}$)**: Elevated upper-left front illumination: `normalize(vec3(-0.4, 0.9, 0.7))`
**Fill Light ($\vec{V}$)**: Camera-aligned light ensuring curvature visibility from all orbit angles.
**Ambient Floor**: Constant $0.38$, ensuring shadows remain rich, saturated, and never black.
**View-Oriented Normals**: Flipping $\vec{N}$ if $\vec{N} \cdot \vec{V} < 0$ enables correct illumination on both sides of thin sheets, Möbius strips, and folding mats.

blocks.text: 2.3 Integration with the Model Primitive
Any `Model` (Box, Sphere, Cylinder, Torus, custom OBJ mesh) can opt into Manim shading either at construction or dynamically at runtime:
Non-Destructive State Backup (pbrMaterialBackup)

When switching from PBR to Manim shading, `Model` caches the user's customized `roughness`, `metallic`, and `specular` properties in `_pbrMaterialBackup`. Calling `usePBRShading()` restores these exact user values rather than resetting to arbitrary defaults. If no custom values were previously set, it falls back to standard physically based non-metallic dielectric constants (`roughness: 1.0`, `metallic: 0.0`, `specular: 0.5`).
3. Polyhedra Edge Treatment: Gouraud Smoothing vs. Hard Crease Normals
When rendering polygonal models such as cubes, tetrahedra, or prisms:

items: **Gouraud / Smooth Averaging**: Averages normals across shared vertices. If adjacent faces meet at a steep dihedral angle ($> 60^\circ$), smooth averaging causes lighting to bend around the corner, creating rounded, smeared, or "pillow" artifacts on sharp geometric edges.
**Hard / Split Normals**: Vertices along creases are duplicated with independent normal vectors pointing perpendicularly to each respective face.

blocks.code:
Smooth Gouraud Normal                       Hard Face Normals
          (Edge Artifact)                        (Crisp Polyhedra Edge)

              \  N  /                                N1 |       / N2
               \ | /                                    |      /
                \|/                                     |     /
      ───────────*───────────                 ──────────*    *───────────
          Face 1    Face 2                       Face 1        Face 2

blocks.text: 4. Automatic 3D Morphing (Morph(from, to))
The `Morph` animation engine handles transitions between two 3D models with 1:1 vertex correspondence:
Canonical Mathematical Morph Families Demonstrated in Retiam

items: **Isometric Catenoid-Helicoid Homotopy (Bonnet Associate Family)**:

blocks.text: *(Strictly preserves the first fundamental form $ds^2 = \cosh^2(v)(du^2 + dv^2)$; every patch deforms without any stretching or shrinking).*

items: **Torus Aperture Homotopy**:

blocks.text: Continuous transition through topological singularities:

blocks.tex: \text{Ring Torus } (R > r) \longrightarrow \text{Horn Torus } (R = r) \longrightarrow \text{Spindle Torus } (R < r) \longrightarrow \text{Degenerate Sphere } (R = 0)

items: **Ribbon & Möbius Strip Homotopy**:

blocks.text: Continuous rotation of the cross-sectional ribbon normal by $\frac{\alpha u}{2}$, transitioning from an untwisted cylindrical band ($\alpha = 0$) to a non-orientable Möbius strip ($\alpha = 2\pi$).

items: **Multi-State Sheet Folding Morph** (`morph_mat_folding.ts`):

blocks.text: Sequencing morphs across 5 states: Flat Mat $\to$ Accordion Pleats $\to$ 180° Book Fold $\to$ Spiral Scroll $\to$ Double Roll.
5. Manual Programmatic Vertex Animation (No Auto-Morph)
While `Morph(from, to)` is ideal for metamorphoses between different geometries, linear vertex interpolation causes severe issues when folding a continuous sheet:

items: At $t = 0.5$, straight-line vertex paths force the folding flap to **shrink and collapse through itself** before re-expanding.
It requires maintaining **two separate entities** in memory.

blocks.text: 5.1 The Solution: Direct In-Place VRAM Updates
Retiam provides direct programmatic vertex manipulation on a **single entity**, executing in-place WebGPU buffer uploads via hardware `writeBuffer`:

blocks.code:
flowchart LR F["User function f(u,v,t)
Kinematic evaluation"] --> A["Typed arrays in place
positions and normals"] A --> G["WebGPU writeBuffer
Hardware VRAM upload"] A -.-> N["Reported zero heap allocations"] G -.-> P["Reported 60–120 FPS"]

blocks.text: 5.2 Core API Methods Added
Model.updateVertices(positions, normals?)
*Defined in [Model.ts](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/Model.ts#L223)*

items: Copies new coordinates directly into `this.geo.mesh.vertices` without re-creating arrays.
Preserves the index buffer and GPU pipeline layout in VRAM.
Flags `this.geo.isDirty = true` to queue a fast WebGPU DMA transfer.

blocks.text: ParametricModel.updateSurface(func, normalFunc?)
*Defined in [ParametricModel.ts](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/ParametricModel.ts#L55)*

items: Re-evaluates $(x, y, z)$ over the existing $(u_i, v_j)$ grid resolution without heap allocation.
Computes surface normals dynamically via central finite-difference tangent cross products:

blocks.tex: \vec{t}_u = \frac{p(u+\epsilon, v) - p(u-\epsilon, v)}{2\epsilon}, \quad \vec{t}_v = \frac{p(u, v+\epsilon) - p(u, v-\epsilon)}{2\epsilon}, \quad \vec{n} = \frac{\vec{t}_v \times \vec{t}_u}{\|\vec{t}_v \times \vec{t}_u\|}

items: Ensures specular highlights, diffuse lighting, and checkerboard shading react realistically as the surface curves.
